subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw permit a persistent operator assertion to bypass the WAL-reset corruption guard for distribution-linked SQLite, and what verification and revalidation contract must accompany it?
rationale: Source inspection can confirm that the bypass is restricted to Node shared-SQLite builds, but only maintainers can decide whether operator risk acceptance is an acceptable long-term data-integrity boundary.

options.title: Accept with guardrails
options.body: Keep the shared-only override, document qualifying vendor evidence and revalidation after SQLite package changes, and require a real affected-image startup transcript before merge.

options.title: Keep strict version enforcement
options.body: Reject the override and require affected distributions or deployment images to supply an explicitly safe SQLite release line.

options.title: Accept persistent assertion
options.body: Merge the boolean override as written and explicitly accept that operators own corruption risk after future shared-library changes.

recommendation.title: Accept with guardrails
recommendation.body: Keep the shared-only override, document qualifying vendor evidence and revalidation after SQLite package changes, and require a real affected-image startup transcript before merge.
